dialog.body: Recreation Department, this is Beth, good morning!

Good morning, Beth. Okay, so I'm calling because I want to buy a memorial bench, and I've called three wrong numbers already this morning, I'm starting to think I should just get a phone book, but anyway my brother always sat down at the water, he walked down there every single day for years, and the family would like a bench with a little plaque in a park near the beach, so I don't know if that's you or somebody else, or if there's a form, or how much it is, or whether there's a list of places where a bench can go.

Well, you got the right number this time! I'm sorry about your brother. Yes, the Recreation Department handles the memorial bench program for the city parks and the beach areas. There's an application, and you'd choose a location, and staff look at whether that spot works.
Okay. And is there a list of the spots or do I pick one and ask?

You can tell us where you'd like it, and we'll let you know if it's available. Some places already have a lot of benches, and some spots can't take one for safety or access reasons. So it helps to give a first choice and maybe a second.
Alright. And the cost, do you have the cost?
The price depends on the bench and the plaque, and I don't have the current number in front of me. The application packet lists it. I can email it to you or mail it, whichever is easier.
Mail is better. Actually, wait, can I pick it up? I'm not far from there.
Sure, you can stop by the office. Heads up, though, the nor'easter is moving in today, so the roads might get messy later. If you're coming, I'd do it this morning.
Yes, I saw that on the news. I'll see how it goes. Can you tell me again what I need to bring, or what the steps are, so I can write it down? I've got a pen now.

Of course. Step one, pick up or request the application. Step two, fill it out with your first and second choice of location and the wording you want on the plaque. Step three, send it back to us, and staff review it. Then we contact you about the approval and the payment.
Okay, hold on. Pick up the application, then first and second location, then the wording, then send it back, then you call me about payment. Is that right?
That's exactly right. Plaque wording usually has a length limit, so keep it short and sweet, and the packet will say how many lines.
Good. Can you say the part about the locations one more time? I only wrote down first and second.
Sure. Give us your first choice and a backup choice, because the first one might not be available. The staff checks each spot before approving.
Okay, got it. Backup choice. And how long does it take after that, do you know?
It varies, and winter is a slower time for installation, so I wouldn't promise a date. They can tell you more once your application is in.
That's fine. Then I'll have you mail it, since the storm might make a mess. Should I give you my address?
Yes please, though I have to ask, what name and mailing address would you like on it?
It's Rosa Mejia, M-E-J-I-A. The address, well, I'd rather pick it up, honestly. I'll just come by Monday when the weather clears. Will the office be open?
We're open Monday, regular hours. I'll leave an application at the front counter with your name on it, so you won't have to wait.
That's very kind. And if I have a question before then, is there a direct number?
You can call back to this same line and ask for me, Beth. If I'm out, someone else will help you.
Okay. My number is 401-555-0152, in case you need me.
Got it, 401-555-0152. I'll note it on the request.
Thank you, Beth. You were the first person who actually knew what I was talking about today.
Happy to help, Rosa. Stay safe in the storm, and we'll see you Monday!
Thank you. Goodbye.
